Theme

Latin word

opera

opera, operae f.

noun, first declension

effort, pains, work freely given; work given or sold; manual labour

In this lexicon

  • effort

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.18.2: maximē autem date operam ut valeātis; Plaut. Poen. 332: et oleum et operam perdidī; Traupman 97: make an effort to be on time, dā operam ut tempestīvē adsīs; Traupman 308: it’s (not) worth the effort, pretium operae (nōn) est; Traupman 110: operam dō ut (nē) (+ subjunctive)

  • labour

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.150: quōrum operae, nōn quōrum artēs emuntur (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • maximē autem date operam ut valeātis, sī nōs vultis valēre

    above all, make every effort to keep well, if you want us to be wellCic. Fam. 14.18.2

    In the entry for effort

  • sī, quantum operae sūmpsistī ut tuus pistor bonum faceret pānem, ejus duodecimam philosophiae dedissēs, ipse bonus jam prīdem essēs factus

    if you had given philosophy a twelfth of the effort you spent getting your baker to make good bread, you would have become good yourself long agoVarro in Gell. 15.19.2

    In the entry for effort

    Then, by heaven, I’ve wasted my lamp oil and my effort.Plaut. Poen. 332
